title: Upholstery spot cleaner
subtitle: A foam-action spray for food stains and marks on fabric sofas and chairs
excerpt: A foaming spray cleaner for fabric upholstery, bicarbonate of soda, white vinegar, a few drops of castile soap, and warm water in a spray bottle. Spritzed on the stain, left to work, then blotted out. Works well on food stains, light oil marks, and general soiling. Test on a hidden area first. Makes one spray bottle (250 ml).
sourceNotes: Upholstery spot cleaning: dilute surfactant (castile soap) lifts grease and protein stains. White vinegar neutralises alkaline stains (pet urine, some food stains) and helps release stain molecules from fibres. Bicarbonate of soda in low concentration (dissolved, not as a paste) aids pH adjustment and mild odour absorption. Never saturate upholstery, excess moisture can cause watermarks, shrinkage in natural fibres, and mould in foam. Blotting (not rubbing) technique is critical: rubbing spreads the stain and damages fibre structure. Pre-test for colourfastness required for all upholstery. Not suitable for silk, velvet, or dry-clean-only fabrics.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be stored in the spray bottle for up to 2 weeks. Shake before use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Use within 2 weeks. The castile soap can separate and the solution may become cloudy. Shake before each use.

glossaryTerms.definition: Pressing a clean cloth onto a stain to absorb moisture and residue, rather than rubbing. Rubbing spreads the stain and can push it deeper into the upholstery fibres; blotting lifts it.

content.text: Upholstery spot cleaner is a dilute bicarbonate, vinegar, and castile soap solution in a spray bottle for fabric sofas and chairs. Spritz a small amount onto the stain, leave for a minute or two, then blot, never rub, with a white cloth. The
technique is important: rubbing spreads the stain and damages the fibres. Always test on a hidden area first. Not for silk, velvet, or dry-clean-only fabric. Makes 250 ml.

items.prepNote: approx. 5 drops; or tea tree EO; for odour

content.text: Combine all ingredients in the spray bottle. The bicarb and vinegar will fizz briefly, this is normal. Swirl gently to combine.
Test on a hidden area of the upholstery and leave 2 minutes to check colourfastness before using on a visible stain.
Spritz 2-3 times onto the stain. Leave for 1-2 minutes.
Press a clean white cloth firmly onto the stain and hold for a few seconds. Lift. Repeat with a fresh part of the cloth, working from the outside of the stain inward.
Leave to air dry. Brush the fibres back into place once dry.
Use within 2 weeks. Shake before each use. Discard if it smells strongly of vinegar or the solution looks discoloured.
